title: One day that isn’t yours
told: a story of the martyrs of Abitinae

card.from: a story of the martyrs of Abitinae
card.keepWhy: One day a week isn’t yours to fill.
sources: Acts of the Martyrs of Abitinae (Acta Saturnini, Dativi et aliorum), Roman Africa, 304: under Diocletian’s persecution, which banned Christian gatherings and ordered the scriptures handed over, a group of Christians of Abitinae (in present-day Tunisia) gathered for the Lord’s supper (dominicum) with the priest Saturninus; they were arrested and taken to Carthage before the proconsul Anulinus; the lector Emeritus said the gathering was held in his house and answered, “sine dominico non possumus” (“we cannot live without the Lord’s day / the Lord’s supper”); many died in prison.
John Paul II, Dies Domini (1998) 46, citing the martyrs of Abitinae; Benedict XVI, homily at Bari, 29 May 2005 (“Without Sunday we cannot live”).
Matthew 28:1; Mark 16:2; Luke 24:1; John 20:1 (the empty tomb on the first day of the week). Revelation 1:10 (the Lord’s day).

Catechism of the Catholic Church 2174-2188 (the Lord’s day; the Sunday obligation, which may be fulfilled on Sunday or the evening of the preceding day; excused for a serious reason such as illness or care of infants, 2180-2181).
Latin dies Domini; Spanish domingo; Italian domenica.
check: The Latin dominicum can mean the Lord’s day or the Lord’s supper; the lesson translates it “Sunday,” following John Paul II and Benedict XVI. Confirm.
The Acts count about forty-nine martyrs; the painting shows “about forty” and the caption says only “a group.” Confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? growing up, did sunday feel like a gift or a chore?
options: that’s honest. lots of people felt that. this story might turn it around.
then you’ll love where this goes.
that’s most weeks now. watch what one day meant to these people.

steps.line: Around the year 304, in a North African town called Abitinae, the Roman emperor banned Christians from meeting. Their holy books were being taken away.
But every Sunday, a group of them still gathered in a house, with their priest, to share the Lord’s supper: the Mass.

steps.q: Soldiers find them gathered together. What do you think happens?
o: They are arrested and taken to the governor
They hide and are never found
The soldiers quietly let them go
steps.why: They’re arrested. And they go calmly, still together.

steps.line: Soldiers found them and took them to the city of Carthage, to stand before the Roman governor.
The governor asked why they had broken the emperor’s order. A man named Emeritus, who had opened his house to them, answered.

steps.why: In Latin, sine dominico non possumus. Dominicum can mean the Lord’s day or the Lord’s supper; for them, the two went together.

steps.line: “Without Sunday, we cannot live.” Many of them never came home. But their words are still quoted by the Church today.

steps.q: They could have prayed alone at home, safely. Why did they keep gathering on Sunday?
o: They hadn’t heard about the ban
Sunday at the table together was life itself
Their priest ordered them to come
steps.why: For them Sunday wasn’t a rule to tick off. It was the day they met the risen Jesus at the table, together.

steps.line: Today, the Church asks Catholics to keep Sunday: Mass on Sunday or Saturday evening, then rest, family, a long meal. Sickness or caring for someone excuses you.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Catholics can keep Sunday at a Saturday evening Mass. Why does that count?
o: Priests can’t fit enough Masses into Sunday
In the Bible’s way of counting, a day begins at evening
Saturday was the old Sabbath, so it carries over
steps.why: “There was evening and there was morning,” says Genesis. The Church’s great days still begin the evening before, so a Saturday night vigil belongs to Sunday.

say: here’s what i love. for them, sunday wasn’t homework. it was the day jesus rose, the first day of the week, and they couldn’t imagine living without it.
catholics call it the lord’s day. the church asks it as an obligation so the gift actually gets opened: left alone, a week fills every hour. one day a week isn’t yours to fill.

steps.q: The Jewish Sabbath is the seventh day. Why would the first Christians gather on Sunday, the first day of the week?
o: It was the day the tomb was found empty
steps.why: All four Gospels put the empty tomb on the first day of the week. So every Sunday is a small Easter.

today.say: this sunday, keep one hour that isn’t yours to fill: mass, if you go, or a long meal, a walk, a call to family. phone face down. if you pray, you can offer the hour to God.
options: good. that’s the gift getting opened.
no pressure. even thinking about it counts. the door is open.
